questions.q: What is the primary policy shift brought by Republic Act 10121 in Philippine disaster management?

choices.A: Focusing exclusively on post-disaster emergency financial aid
choices.B: Banning all construction in high-density urban areas
choices.C: Shifting from reactive emergency response to proactive risk reduction and resilience
choices.D: Eliminating natural hazards along shoreline provinces

questions.q: A town vulnerable to earthquakes may not be vulnerable to typhoons. What key characteristic of vulnerability does this illustrate?
Why is population density a critical factor in evaluating community disaster risk compared to simple population size?

choices.A: It measures the total financial assets of a city
choices.B: It counts the exact number of emergency responders
choices.C: It determines the physical length of coastlines
choices.D: It reflects spatial congestion, which can cause severe escape bottlenecks during emergencies

questions.q: In your own words, describe what VULNERABILITY means based on DRRM principles.
questions.reference: Vulnerability is a state of being at risk or susceptible to the damaging effects of a hazard, determining the ability to predict, cope with, resist, and recover.

questions.q: Drag each term into the description it matches.

slots.desc: The total count of individuals inhabiting a space at the exact same time (e.g., 65,000 residents).
How people are spread out across a land area (e.g., 80% on farmlands vs. 20% on a riverbank).
The number of individuals living in an area relative to the physical size of that area (e.g., 20,000 people per km²).
